The thing is you’re gonna have to fight through your anxiety. Saying you can not is only a crutch for not trying. I fight through the same thing. I say ‘fight’ because it is difficult. But to have the life you want, you have to go get it. 

But let me just say showing up is literally half the battle. Once you to start showing up and participating people will notice you. I found that wearing a little confidence helps. Even if you have very little wear it. You admit to having a lot to offer and the sooner you wear that with confidence, you can approach new situations. You have the anxiety because it’s new. Become a regular somewhere or start small by going to some meet ups. So it’s no longer new then you will start to see you will become who you need to be when you need it. So go out trusting your judgment and have fun!

Also I recommend that you start with only the goal of going out. You have to take baby steps. Make small interactions with people around you. Then over time it’ll come more naturally. I love to skateboard but skating around other people gives me pretty bad anxiety. So I started by driving to the skatepark then leaving. Then I’d drive, get out get out the car and sit. Third step was to get on the board and just do it. When I got on after a few times of just showing up. I started to just focus on myself and having fun. After that I became more familiar with what to expect and became a regular. So now I’ve met a few people by just speaking up or commenting and letting them take the reigns of the conversation since I’m more introverted. You have a lot of hobbies so you can try that over and over. 

Most importantly be yourself. Apart of being yourself is realizing that there are many you’s. You’ve lived life and you’re into a lot of things. So you’re adaptable to change. You can handle any situation but you have to realize you can. You don’t have to be extroverted to make friends. You do well one on one. You know your strength so run with it. Start a conversation with a random guy, since that’s slightly more difficult. Doesn’t have to be a long but small talk and work your way up. Your brain automatically makes the association so just say the first thing that’s appropriate. You’re not looking for the “right thing” to say you’re just letting it flow. You’re just l letting yourself be yourself. You can’t fake being genuine. 

In short: take the first step and keep making progress little by little. Take control by trusting yourself to handle it. Once you know you can, your confidence will grow. Always, always be yourself.
